entries.text: Be still, and know that I am God.
For God hath not given us the spirit of fear; but of power, and of love, and of a sound mind.
I can do all things through Christ which strengtheneth me.
Love is patient, love is kind. It does not envy, it does not boast, it is not proud.
Love bears all things, believes all things, hopes all things, endures all things.
There is no fear in love; but perfect love casteth out fear.
The Lord is my shepherd; I shall not want.
He maketh me to lie down in green pastures: he leadeth me beside the still waters.
To every thing there is a season, and a time to every purpose under the heaven.
A time to weep, and a time to laugh; a time to mourn, and a time to dance.
Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest.
And now abideth faith, hope, charity, these three; but the greatest of these is charity.
Consider the lilies of the field, how they grow; they toil not, neither do they spin.
Take therefore no thought for the morrow: for the morrow shall take thought for the things of itself.
Blessed are the meek: for they shall inherit the earth.
Blessed are the peacemakers: for they shall be called the children of God.
I am fearfully and wonderfully made.
Thou hast beset me behind and before, and laid thine hand upon me.
Weeping may endure for a night, but joy cometh in the morning.
The Lord is my light and my salvation; whom shall I fear?
Trust in the Lord with all thine heart; and lean not unto thine own understanding.
A soft answer turneth away wrath: but grievous words stir up anger.
Pleasant words are as an honeycomb, sweet to the soul, and health to the bones.
As iron sharpeneth iron; so a man sharpeneth the countenance of his friend.
A merry heart doeth good like a medicine.
They that wait upon the Lord shall renew their strength; they shall mount up with wings as eagles.
For I know the thoughts that I think toward you, thoughts of peace, and not of evil, to give you an expected end.
What doth the Lord require of thee, but to do justly, and to love mercy, and to walk humbly?
Ask, and it shall be given you; seek, and ye shall find; knock, and it shall be opened unto you.
Judge not, that ye be not judged.
Let not your heart be troubled.
Peace I leave with you, my peace I give unto you: not as the world giveth, give I unto you.
Ye are the light of the world.
Love thy neighbour as thyself.
Greater love hath no man than this, that a man lay down his life for his friends.
The truth shall make you free.
I am my beloved's, and my beloved is mine.
Set me as a seal upon thine heart, as a seal upon thine arm: for love is strong as death.
The Lord is my strength and my song.
This is the day which the Lord hath made; we will rejoice and be glad in it.
